items.title: I don’t expect superposition in transformer MLP neurons
items.summary: The author believes that superposition-type compression exists in the residual stream of transformer models but not in the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neurons. This separation is argued to reduce noise and is more useful because information flow through the residual stream is more critical. Superposition in the MLP is seen as introducing too much noise, requiring costly error correction that is not justified. The author suggests that feature encoding might be fundamentally different from the superposition paradigm, focusing instead on feature geometry. Ultimately, the author finds the concept of superposition less central to understanding feature embedding in large language models.
items.audio_script: From AI Alignment Forum, "I don’t expect superposition in transformer MLP neurons". This segment addresses the existence of superposition-type compression within transformer model architectures, finding a distinction between the residual stream and the Multi-Layer Perceptron neurons. The research argues that superposition-type compression is present in the residual stream of transformer models but absent in the MLP neurons, suggesting this separation reduces noise and is more beneficial as information flow through the residual stream is deemed more critical. The analysis posits that superposition within the MLP introduces excessive noise requiring unnecessary error correction, and that feature encoding may be better understood through feature geometry rather than the superposition paradigm. This finding suggests a reevaluation of the role of superposition in understanding feature embedding within large language models. The results indicate a potential shift in theoretical focus for feature representation in advanced neural networks.

items.title: Tencent Open-Sources DFly2: Speculative Decoding That Reuses the Target’s Sparse KV Cache
items.summary: Tencent open-sourced DFly2, a speculative decoding drafter designed for natively sparse Large Language Models. DFly2 achieves this by reusing the target model's sparse Key-Value (KV) cache and indexer selections, eliminating the need for a separate draft KV cache. Benchmarks show DFly2 achieves up to 81% more throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 64K context, while also outperforming DSpark on long-context and agentic workloads. The method reduces memory overhead for draft caches, allowing more requests to be served within the same memory pool. DFly2 is integrated into Tencent's Hy4 flash and can be trained on other sparse models using AngelSpec.

items.title: How to Calculate Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) in E-Commerce
items.summary: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) is a unit-economics metric estimating the total profit a business can expect from a single customer relationship over its lifespan. It shifts focus from individual transactions to the cumulative value incorporating sales, margins, frequency, retention, and acquisition costs. Calculating CLV involves summing discounted future revenue minus costs, utilizing models like Buy 'Til You Die (BTYD) to estimate customer lifespan in non-contractual settings. Operationalizing CLV requires mapping revenue and costs to lifecycle events, identifying High-Value Actions (HVAs), and using behavioral segmentation like RFM. Ultimately, effective CLV management involves strategically investing in interventions where the marginal CLV uplift exceeds the cost of the action.

items.title: Code Mode vs. Tool Calling Benchmarks Find a 16-Tool Crossover
items.summary: Code Mode moves execution outside the context window by having the model write and execute code, which reduces context load for intermediate results. It demonstrates significant cost and time savings, especially for repetitive or fan-out tasks, with a crossover point around 16 tools for single-step tasks. For fan-out tasks, Code Mode is consistently cheaper and faster, reducing costs by up to 120 times compared to plain tool calling. However, Code Mode is not a universal solution, as it can fail on complex multi-step tasks or with less capable models. Therefore, Code Mode is most beneficial when handling many tools and item-heavy workloads, not as a default for all agent tasks.

items.title: Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark
items.summary: Order in benchmark text is important because models trained on it might learn the sequence. A statistical method using sequential shards and permutations allows for testing if a model prefers the original order. A high z-score suggests a model has memorized the order, indicating potential contamination. Experiments with six real models and several statistical tests yielded no significant results. Limitations exist due to potential blind spots regarding order learning and sample size.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark".
